walkthroughs.body_html:
Galaxies & Cosmology — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Galaxies & Cosmology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Galaxies & Cosmology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: The Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below the Sun's apparent position.
Because clouds block them.
Straight lines that bend.
Eclipses happen randomly.

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It is the largest stage of a star's life.
It is the hottest stage.
Because clouds block them.
It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Steady-state model”?
options: Discredited rival model (Hoyle, Bondi, Gold 1948) where the universe is unchanging on large scales.
Brief phase (10^-36 to 10^-32 s) of exponential expansion that smoothed and flattened the universe.
~380,000 years after the Big Bang, electrons combined with nuclei, freeing photons.
Stretching of space itself, increasing distances between galaxies over time.
